properties.Title: Yoga Sutras of Patanjali (BonGiovanni translation)
properties.Key Context: Full English rendering of the Yoga Sutras. 1.2 defines yoga as restraining the thought-streams (vrittis) of the mind; 1.5-1.11 list the kinds of thought-streams (incl. sleep, memory); 1.12-1.14 say they are controlled by practice and non-attachment, practice being sustained effort toward steadiness.
properties.Credibility notes: Hosted on sacred-texts.com; BonGiovanni is a modern, non-academic translation. Cross-check wording against a scholarly translation.

properties.Title: Katha Upanishad I.3 (Max Müller, SBE 15)
properties.Key Context: Chariot analogy: the Self sits in the chariot, the body is the chariot, the intellect (buddhi) the charioteer, the mind (manas) the reins, and the senses the horses. Following verses contrast one whose mind is never firm with one who has understanding and a controlled mind.
properties.Credibility notes: Max Müller's Sacred Books of the East translation (1884), public domain, standard but dated.

properties.Title: Bhagavad Gita 6.35 - mind restrained by practice and detachment
properties.Key Context: Sanskrit, word-by-word gloss and translation of BG 6.35: Krishna agrees the mind is restless and very difficult to restrain, but says it can be controlled by practice (abhyasa) and detachment (vairagya). Parallels Yoga Sutra 1.12.
properties.Credibility notes: Translation/commentary by Swami Mukundananda (devotional lineage). Verse text reliable; commentary is interpretive.

properties.Title: Manas (mind and mental health) - Charak Samhita Online
properties.Key Context: Compiles Charaka Samhita passages on manas with citations: life (ayu) is the combination of body, senses, mind and soul (Sutra Sthana 1/42), and mind is one of three pillars of the person. Covers mind's functions, its role in sleep, and restraining the mind from harmful objects as a traditional form of psychotherapy.
properties.Credibility notes: Charak Samhita Research, Training and Development Centre wiki; cites verse references. Secondary compilation of primary text, verify key verses.

properties.Title: Vivekachudamani commentary - antahkarana (manas, buddhi, chitta, ahamkara)
properties.Key Context: Explains Vivekachudamani vv. 95-96: the inner organ (antahkarana) is called manas when cogitating alternatives, buddhi when deciding, chittam when storing memory, and ahamkara as the 'I' behind these. Notes Panchadasi 1.20 names only manas and buddhi.
properties.Credibility notes: Translation/notes by S. N. Sastri on sanskritdocuments.org; traditional Advaita perspective.

properties.Title: Abhidhammattha Sangaha, Ch. II: Compendium of Mental States (cetasikas)
properties.Key Context: States that 52 mental states (cetasikas) arise and perish with consciousness, sharing its object and basis. Discusses key factors such as feeling (vedana), perception (sanna) and volition (cetana), and their classification.
properties.Credibility notes: Narada Thera's translation and notes of the Theravada Abhidhamma manual, hosted on palikanon.com.

properties.Title: Mind in Indian Buddhist Philosophy (SEP)
properties.Key Context: Surveys ~15 centuries of Indian Buddhist theories of mind. Buddhists, like other Indian philosophers, see mind as interrelated faculties and processes, but deny a substantive enduring self; theories centre on not-self (anatta).
properties.Credibility notes: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, peer-reviewed reference.

properties.Title: Abhidharma (SEP)
properties.Key Context: Explains how post-Buddha scholastic schools developed Abhidharma as a systematic method for organizing the Buddha's teachings, understood as 'higher' or 'further' teaching. Useful background on how mind and mental factors are analysed into dharmas.
properties.Credibility notes: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy; substantively revised Mar 2026.

properties.Title: Yoga Sutras of Patanjali (IEP)
properties.Key Context: Describes classical Yoga as meditative practice culminating in consciousness free from all active or discursive thought, and ultimately aware only of itself; this is the classical means to liberation. Notes the Yoga Sutras were treated across schools as the orthodox meditation manual.

properties.Title: Sankhya (IEP)
properties.Key Context: Classical Samkhya (Samkhya Karika, c. 350 CE) is a dualism of Prakriti (Nature) and many purushas (persons). Nature has three gunas: sattva (light, intelligence), rajas (change, passion), tamas (inertia, dullness), and comprises the gross body and subtle body, the framework from which buddhi, ahamkara and manas evolve.

properties.Title: Human nature: Indian perspective revisited (PMC)
properties.Key Context: Reviews Indian views of mind for psychiatry: Advaita's antahkarana has four divisions (manas, buddhi, ahamkara, citta), often reduced to two; Samkhya has three (buddhi, ahamkara, manas), with manas as the eleventh indriya. Relates these to Western and transpersonal psychology.
properties.Credibility notes: Open-access article in Indian Journal of Psychiatry (2011), on PubMed Central.

properties.Title: Importance of Manas Tattva: A searchlight in Yoga Darshana (PMC)
properties.Key Context: Reviews manas in Yoga and Ayurvedic texts. Per the Yoga Sutra tradition, chitta comprises buddhi, ahamkara and manas; chitta vritti is the aggregate of perceiving and memory processes, followed by buddhi vritti and ahamkara vritti. Notes Charaka places the seat of manas in the heart (hridaya).
properties.Credibility notes: Open-access review in AYU journal, on PubMed Central; textual review rather than empirical study.

properties.Title: The Abhidhamma in Practice (N. K. G. Mendis)
properties.Key Context: Practical introduction to the four ultimate realities (citta, cetasikas, rupa, nibbana) and the 52 mental factors, which arise and cease with consciousness and share its object and base. Explains factors such as mindfulness (sati) and how close observation distinguishes wholesome and unwholesome roots.
properties.Credibility notes: Buddhist Publication Society Wheel booklet (No. 322) on Access to Insight; expository, not peer-reviewed.

properties.Title: Samkhya Part Five: Samkhya Karika continued (sreenivasarao's blog)
properties.Key Context: Walks through the Samkhya Karika's evolution of Prakriti: buddhi/mahat first, then ahamkara ('I' and 'mine'), then manas and the ten senses. Buddhi, ahamkara and manas form the inner organ (antahkarana); manas coordinates sensations and thoughts.
properties.Credibility notes: Well-regarded independent blog with textual references; not peer-reviewed.

properties.Title: Samkhya Karika verse 27 - manas (Centre for Yoga Studies)
properties.Key Context: Word-by-word study of Samkhya Karika 27: manas is the eleventh indriya and is deliberative (sankalpaka), coordinating the other senses. The variety of experience is explained by changes in the gunas.
properties.Credibility notes: Teacher-run Viniyoga study site (Paul Harvey); helpful glossary, interpretive.

properties.Title: What is the difference/relation between Chitta and Manas? (Hinduism Stack Exchange)
properties.Key Context: The accepted answer says the terms are used loosely: manas usually means deliberation and citta means recollection. It quotes Swami Satprakashananda's four functions (manas deliberates, buddhi determines, ahamkara 'I know', citta recalls) using an example of seeing a chair, and notes Vedanta-sara folds ahamkara into manas and citta into buddhi.
properties.Credibility notes: Community Q&A (2018); answer quotes a published Ramakrishna Order author. Use only as a pointer.
